capabilities: write spreadsheet-style formulas (e.g. =SUM(B2:B4)) into table cells
bake evaluated results into cells with a command
preserve original formulas in inline %%...%% comments
restore a baked cell to its bare formula for re-editing
disambiguation: Not a live spreadsheet; formulas only evaluate when a command is run, baking results into the cell text rather than recalculating automatically.
extras: Development was LLM-assisted (Claude Code with Sonnet 5), with the author stating they reviewed and modified all code; no usage examples or screenshots are provided.
motivation: The author built it for personal use so tables can hold computed data in plain text for portability where a dedicated spreadsheet is overkill, and as an exercise in LLM-assisted development with Claude Code.
problem: Markdown tables are static text, so simple calculations require copying data into a separate spreadsheet and pasting results back.
summary: Spreadsheet-style formula engine for Markdown tables that bakes computed values into cells while keeping the formula in an inline comment.
